raw_text:
Here’s a clear, week-by-week summary that pulls together the 12-week strength plan, intensified Phase 2, cardio, mobility, Saturday finisher, and nutrition into one place. It’s designed for a 27-year-old beginner training in a small flat with a yoga mat and doorway pull-up bar.

Global structure
- Training split: 3 strength sessions/week (A, B, C), optional Saturday Finisher (fun 20–30 min), 2–3 cardio sessions/week, daily short mobility.
- Phases: Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Progression/Intensity (Weeks 5–8), Intensification/Peak (Weeks 9–12).
- Session length: 45–60 minutes (strength), 15–30 minutes (cardio), 8–10 minutes (daily mobility).
- Progression: Add reps within ranges first; then increase leverage/ROM/tempo; keep 1–2 reps in reserve (RIR), push last set to 0–1 RIR selectively.

Warm-up before every strength session (8–10 min)
- 1 min 90/90 or crocodile breathing
- Cat-camel x6, world’s greatest stretch x3/side, 90/90 hip switches x6/side
- Activation: glute bridge 2x8, scap push-ups 1x10, dead bug 1x8/side
- 1–2 easy ramp-up sets of first upper and lower movements

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Learn patterns, build tolerance, establish volume with controlled tempo.

Week 1
- Session A: Split squat 3x8/side; incline/elevated push-up 3x8–10; doorway/table row 4x6–8; glute bridge 3x10–12; dead bug 3x6/side; side plank 3x20–30s/side
- Session B: Box/chair squat 4x6–8; elevated push-up 4x6–8; assisted chin-up 5x3–5; hip hinge wall taps 3x10; hollow hold (tuck) 3x15–25s; passive-to-active hang 4x10s active
- Session C: Reverse lunge 3x8/side; pike push-up (hands elevated) 3x6–8; horizontal towel/doorframe row 4x6–8; single-leg bridge 3x8/side; plank 3x25–40s; prone Y-T-W 2x8 each

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps where clean. If at top range, slow eccentrics to 4s or add 1 set to main lower move. Chin-ups: +1 total rep vs Week 1.

Week 3
- Progress leverage/ROM: lower push-up elevation; slower row eccentrics; add 1s pauses (squat/lunge bottoms); 2s bridge top holds. Chin-ups 5x4–6 assisted.

Week 4
- Overreach then mini-deload: Sessions A/B push to top rep ranges (0–1 RIR), Session C reduce volume by ~20%. Chin-up AMRAP assisted test (leave 1 rep in reserve). Record.

Phase 2: Progression/Intensity (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Harder leverage, clusters, pauses, longer eccentrics; drive strength without equipment. Rest 90–150s on big sets. Most final sets 0–1 RIR.

Week 5
- Session A: Bulgarian split squat 5x5–6/side; push-up (low elevation) 5x5–8 with 4–1–1 first 3 sets; assisted chin-up 6x3 (2s top, 3–4s down); single-leg RDL 4x6–8 (2s bottom); hollow 3x25–35s; scap pulls 4x6
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 6x4 (5s down, 2s pause); pike push-up 5x4–6 (4s down, 1s pause); row 5x6–8 with 3s mid-range iso on last rep; hip thrust (sofa) 4x8–10 (3s top); dead bug 3x10/side; Y-T-W 2x10 each
- Session C: Front-foot-elevated reverse lunge 5x6–8/side; close-grip push-up (elev.) 4x6–8 + 20–30s isometric; chin-up eccentrics 6x2–3 (6–8s); hamstring walkouts 4x8–12; side plank 3x35–45s

Week 6
- Session A: Bulgarians 5x6/side + 1s bottom pause; push-up clusters 4 rounds (3–4 reps + 15–20s + 3–4 reps); assisted chin-up 7x2–3 (2s top, 4s down); single-leg RDL 4x8; hollow (one arm OH) 3x25–35s; active hang 3x30–40s
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 6x4–5; pike push-up clusters 4 rounds (2–3 + 15–20s + 2–3); row 5x6 (4s down); hip thrust 4x8–10 (3s top, last set to 1 RIR); dead bug 3x10/side; wall slides 2x12
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 5x7–8/side; push-up mechanical drop set x3 rounds (hard 4–6 → easier 4–6 → 10–15s iso); chin-up partials top-half 5x2–3 then 1 slow 8–10s eccentric; walkouts 4x10–12; side plank hip lifts 3x10–12/side

Week 7
- Session A: Bulgarians 6x5/side (1s bottom); push-up strength 6x4–6 (3–4s down, 1s pause); chin-up singles 8–10 with least assist (3–4s down; last two add 2s top hold); single-leg RDL 4x6–8 (4s down); hollow rocks 3x12–18
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 7x3–4 (6s down, 2s pause); pike push-up 5x3–5 (4–5s down, last set AMRAP to technical limit); row 5x5–6 (4s down + 1s top pause); hip thrust 4x6–8 (3s top); dead bug 3x10/side
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 5x6–8/side (last set to 1 RIR); push-up eccentrics 4x3–5 (5–6s down + 2s pause) then 1 back-off AMRAP at easier elevation; chin-up eccentrics 6x2 (8–10s) + 1 max top hold; walkouts 4x10–12

Week 8 (deload/consolidate)
- Session A: Bulgarians 4x5–6; push-up 4x4–6 (same elevation); assisted chin-up 5x2–3; single-leg RDL 3x6–8; hollow 2x25–35s; active hang 2x30–40s
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 5x3–4 (4s down); pike push-up 4x3–5; row 4x6–8; hip thrust 3x8–10; dead bug 2x10/side
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 4x6–8/side; push-up back-off 3x6–10 (easier elevation); chin-up eccentrics 4x2 (6s); walkouts 3x8–10
- End-of-week markers: Max floor push-ups or lowest elevation; max assisted chin-ups set; Bulgarian split squat AMRAP to parallel (cap 20).

Phase 3: Intensification/Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Push toward unassisted chin-ups, strong floor push-ups, deeper single-leg strength; slightly lower volume with higher difficulty.

Week 9
- Session A: Bulgarians 5x6/side (last set AMRAP to 1 RIR); push-up floor or low elev. 5x5–8; chin-up clusters: 5 rounds of (1–2 reps, 20–30s, 1–2 reps); hip thrust 4x8–10 (3s final rep hold); hollow 3x25–35s; active hang 3x30–45s
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 6x4 (5s down); pike push-up (deficit if ready) 4x5–6; horizontal row hard angle 4x6–8; single-leg RDL 4x8/side (2s bottom); dead bug 3x10/side; scap wall slides 2x10
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 4x10/side; diamond push-up (appropriate elevation) 4x6–8; chin-up eccentrics 6x2 (6–8s) + 1 timed chin-over-bar hold; walkouts 3x10–12; side plank hip lifts 3x10/side

Week 10
- Add +1 rep/set on push-ups if clean (or feet elevation/pauses if at 8s). Accumulate 30+ total chin-up reps (mix clusters/assists/eccentrics). Lower: deeper ROM or +1 rep, last set AMRAP 1 RIR for Bulgarians/lunges. Keep rows/pike challenging via tempo.

Week 11
- Strength emphasis (lower reps, higher difficulty):
  - Push-up: 6x4–6 (2–3s down, brief bottom pause)
  - Chin-up: 8–10 singles (least assist) with 60–90s rest; last two add 5–10s top hold
  - Rows: 5x6 (4s down)
  - Lower body: 4–5x6–8 (tempo/ROM)
  - Core: Hollow rocks 3x12–20; tall-kneeling anti-rotation press (towel vs doorframe) 3x10s/side

Week 12 (peak/test/deload blend)
- Reduce sets by ~30%, keep effort high (1–2 RIR). Test mid-week:
  - Max clean floor push-ups
  - Chin-up status: 1 unassisted? If not, max assisted + best 8–10s eccentric
  - Split squat AMRAP to parallel (cap 25)

Cardio plan (fits all phases)

  - Session 1: 18–25 min steady (RPE 4–5) – brisk marching, step-ups, shadowboxing

- Weeks 5–8: 2–3 sessions/week
  - Session 1: 25–30 min steady (RPE 5)

- Weeks 9–12: 2–3 sessions/week

Saturday finisher (choose one track weekly, 20–30 min, RPE 6–8)
- Track A: Pull-Up Playground (assisted singles/isos/eccentrics + row/core EMOM + hang game)
- Track B: Push Party + Pump (mechanical drop sets, triceps/delt EMOM, core tag)

- Track D: Full-Body Flow AMRAP (balanced circuit with chins, push-ups, lunges, core, hangs)

Mobility routine
- Daily Short (8–10 min): breathing reset → cat-camel → thread-the-needle → hip 90/90 switches → world’s greatest stretch → ankle rocks → scap CARs → doorway pec stretch → wrist prep → downshift.
- Deeper Reset (20–25 min, 1–2x/week): adds open book, contract–relax for hips/hamstrings, hip flexor/quad, ankle assist, wall slides, Y-T-W, neck hygiene, box breathing.

Nutrition overview (pair with training)
- Calories: BW(kg) × 33–36 kcal/day (or start ~2,600–2,800 kcal/day); adjust ±150–200 kcal based on 2-week trends.

- 12-week focus: Weeks 1–2 consistency; Weeks 3–4 peri-workout carbs; Weeks 5–6 fiber variety; Weeks 7–8 leucine-rich protein; Weeks 9–10 sleep + pre-bed protein; Weeks 11–12 maintain intake that fuels best training.

Equipment roadmap (if he wants to buy later)

Here’s a comprehensive 12-week strength program designed for a beginner training in a small flat with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. The focus is building fundamental movement patterns, progressively overloading with bodyweight variations, and improving joint resilience. Frequency is 3 sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri). Each session lasts ~45–60 minutes. Progression is built-in; if he misses reps, he repeats the week or uses the regression noted. Warm-ups, tempos, and rest times included. Nutrition and recovery guidelines follow at the end.

Overview
- Phases: Foundation (Weeks 1–4), Progression (Weeks 5–8), Intensification (Weeks 9–12)
- Weekly Structure: 3 full-body sessions (A, B, C). Optional short accessory/conditioning finisher.
- Main movement categories: Push (horizontal/vertical), Pull (horizontal/vertical), Squat pattern, Hip hinge, Core (anti-extension/anti-rotation), Scapular/shoulder health.
- Progression keys: Increase reps toward top of range; then add tempo difficulty, range of motion, or leverage before adding volume. Rest 60–120s for compound sets.
- Tempo notation: e.g., 3-0-1 = 3s eccentric, 0s pause, 1s concentric.

Warm-Up Template for Every Session (8–10 min)
- Breathing/reset: 1 minute 90/90 breathing or crocodile breathing.
- Mobility: Cat-camel x6, world’s greatest stretch x3/side, 90/90 hip switches x6/side.
- Activation: Glute bridge 2x8 (2-1-2), scap push-ups 1x10, dead bug 1x8/side.
- Movement prep: 2 sets of the first main lower and upper exercises at easier variations.

Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: Groove technique, build joint tolerance, establish consistent volume. Focus on full range, controlled tempo, and leaving 2–3 reps in reserve (RIR).

Week structure: Same exercises; progress by reps within ranges. If top of range is hit with solid form, progress variation the next week as indicated.

Week 1 Sessions
Session A
- A1 Split Squat (rear-foot on floor) 3x8/side, tempo 3-1-1, rest 75s
- A2 Incline Pike Hand-Elevated Push-Up (hands on countertop/sofa) 3x8–10, 3-1-1, rest 75s
- B1 Doorway Row (towel-assisted under bar or sturdy doorframe row) 4x6–8, 3-1-1, rest 90s
- B2 Glute Bridge 3x10–12, 2-1-2, rest 60s
- C1 Dead Bug 3x6/side, slow and controlled
- C2 Forearm Side Plank 3x20–30s/side

Session B
- A1 Box Squat to Sofa/Chair (sit back, light touch) 4x6–8, 3-1-1
- A2 Push-Up (hands elevated) 4x6–8, 3-1-1
- B1 Assisted Chin-Up (foot on stool/one leg lightly on floor) 5x3–5, 3-1-1, rest 90–120s
- B2 Hip Hinge Drill: Hip Hinge Wall Taps 3x10 (patterning)
- C1 Hollow Body Hold (tuck) 3x15–25s
- C2 Face Pulls (band substitute not available) → Scap Retractions Hang: Passive hang to active hold 4x10s active from the bar

Session C
- A1 Reverse Lunge 3x8/side, 3-1-1
- A2 Pike Push-Up (elevated hands) 3x6–8, 3-1-1
- B1 Horizontal Towel Row Under Table/Bar (if safe) or Doorframe Row 4x6–8
- B2 Single-Leg Hip Bridge 3x8/side, 2-1-2
- C1 Plank 3x25–40s
- C2 Prone Y-T-W (bodyweight) 2x8 each position, control

Week 2
- Add 1–2 reps per set if technique is clean. If already at top, slow the eccentric to 4s on push/pull, or add a set to the main lower exercise (one extra set).
- Keep assisted chin-ups: aim +1 rep total vs Week 1.

Week 3
- Progress difficulty:
  - Push-Ups: lower hand elevation slightly.
  - Rows: increase range, slower 4s eccentrics.
  - Squats/Lunges: add a 1s pause at the bottom.
  - Bridges: add 2s hold at top.
- Volume: Maintain sets, stay 1–2 RIR. Chin-ups: 5x4–6 assisted.

Week 4
- Slight overload then deload within week:
  - Sessions A/B: push to top of rep ranges (0–1 RIR).
  - Session C: reduce volume by 20% (one fewer set per movement), normal tempo.
  - Chin-ups test: AMRAP assisted set after prescribed sets (stop 1 rep before failure). Record.

Phase 2: Progression (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: Increase intensity via harder leverage, introduce negatives and isometrics, consolidate pulling strength, begin unassisted reps where possible.

Adjustments:
- Introduce eccentric-emphasis and isometric holds.
- Begin working toward full push-ups, pike presses, and chin-ups with band/towel assistance or foot assist.
- Add hip hinge loading via tempo and range (Romanian pattern with single-leg variations).

Week 5 Sessions
Session A
- A1 Bulgarian Split Squat (rear foot elevated on sofa edge) 4x6–8/side, 3-1-1
- A2 Push-Up (lower elevation or floor with knee support) 4x6–8, 3-1-1
- B1 Assisted Chin-Up 6x3–5, 3-1-1; add 2–3s chin-over-bar hold last rep each set
- B2 Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift (bodyweight reach) 3x8/side, 3-1-1
- C1 Dead Bug 3x8/side
- C2 Active Hang Scap Pulls 4x5 with 3s hold down

Session B
- A1 Tempo Box Squat to Chair (4s down, 1s pause) 5x5–6
- A2 Pike Push-Up (hips elevated on sofa, hands on floor) 4x5–7
- B1 Doorway/Table Row 4x8–10 (last rep 3s isometric mid-range)
- B2 Hip Thrust (shoulders on sofa) 3x10–12, 2-2-2
- C1 Hollow Body (one leg extended) 3x20–30s
- C2 Prone Y-T-W 2x10 each

Session C
- A1 Reverse Lunge (front foot elevated on book for ROM) 4x8/side
- A2 Close-Grip Push-Up (elevated) 3x6–8
- B1 Chin-Up Eccentrics (jump up, 5s down) 5x2–3; rest 120s
- B2 Hamstring Walkouts (from bridge) 3x6–10
- C1 Side Plank 3x30–40s/side
- C2 Wrist/Elbow Prehab: Wrist rocks, forearm stretch 2 min total

Week 6
- Add 1 rep per set where possible. Chin-ups: accumulate 20–25 quality total reps across sets (assisted + eccentrics). Push-ups: aim for first clean floor reps if capable; otherwise lower elevation again.
- Hinge: Single-leg RDL add 2s bottom pause.

Week 7
- Intensify:
  - Bulgarian Split Squat add 1s pause at bottom; sets 5x6 each.
  - Pike Push-Up: elevate hips higher, increase ROM.
  - Rows: feet further forward under table/doorframe angle to increase difficulty.
  - Chin-ups: 4xAMRAP assisted leaving 1 rep in reserve; then 3x3 controlled eccentrics (5–6s).
- Core: Hollow body full tuck 3x25–35s.

Week 8 (Consolidation/Deload)
- Reduce total volume by ~25% (fewer sets) but keep intensity (same variations, stop 1–2 RIR).
- Test markers at end of week:
  - Max strict push-ups on floor (or lowest elevation possible).
  - Max assisted chin-ups in one set.
  - Bulgarian split squat AMRAP at bodyweight to parallel, 1 set/side (cap at 20).

Phase 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Push toward unassisted chin-ups/pull-ups, strong floor push-ups, deeper single-leg strength, and robust core. More cluster sets and isometric work.

Week 9 Sessions
Session A
- A1 Bulgarian Split Squat 5x6/side, 3-1-1; last set AMRAP to 1 RIR
- A2 Push-Up (floor or minimal elevation) 5x5–8, 3-0-1
- B1 Chin-Up Cluster (assisted or partial ROM): 5 rounds of [1–2 reps, rest 20–30s, 1–2 reps], then 2 min rest between rounds
- B2 Hip Thrust (sofa) 4x8–10 with 3s top hold last rep
- C1 Hollow Body (one arm overhead) 3x25–35s
- C2 Active Hang 3x30–45s

Session B
- A1 Tempo Chair Squat 6x4 (5s down, 1s pause, fast up)
- A2 Pike Push-Up (deficit using books under hands if ready) 4x5–6
- B1 Horizontal Row (feet elevated on chair if safe) 4x6–8; if not possible, slow negatives 4s
- B2 Single-Leg RDL Reach 4x8/side with 2s bottom pause
- C1 Dead Bug 3x10/side
- C2 Scapular Wall Slides 2x10

Session C
- A1 Reverse Lunge (front foot elevated) 4x10/side
- A2 Diamond Push-Up (elevated or floor) 4x6–8
- B1 Chin-Up Eccentrics 6x2 (6–8s down); finish with 1 max timed chin-over-bar hold
- B2 Hamstring Walkouts 3x10–12
- C1 Side Plank Hip Lifts 3x10/side
- C2 Wrist/elbow prehab 2–3 min

Week 10
- Push-Up: aim +1 rep per set; if doing 8s, elevate feet slightly for added load or add 2s pause at bottom.
- Chin-Up: accumulate 30+ total quality reps across clusters/assists/eccentrics. Try partial ROM unassisted reps from top half if possible.
- Lower body: Add 1 rep per set or deeper ROM; last set AMRAP to 1 RIR on Bulgarians and lunges.

Week 11
- Strength focus with lower total reps, higher difficulty:
  - Push-Up: 6x4–6, 2–3s eccentric, brief pause at bottom.
  - Chin-Up: 8–10 singles (assisted as lightly as possible) with 60–90s rest; add 5–10s top hold on last two singles.
  - Rows: 5x6 slower eccentrics.
  - Squat/lunge patterns maintain 4–5x6–8 heavy (via tempo/ROM).
- Core: Hollow rocks 3x12–20, Pallof press substitute: tall-kneeling anti-rotation press with towel isometric vs doorframe 3x10s/side.

Week 12 (Peak/Test/Deload blend)
- Reduce sets by ~30%, keep effort high (1–2 RIR). Mid-week testing.
- Testing suggestions:
  - Max clean floor push-ups (strict, chest to deck, no sag).
  - Chin-up status: Can he do 1 unassisted? If not, max assisted reps + 1 best 8–10s eccentric.
  - Split squat AMRAP set/side to parallel (cap 25).
  - Hollow hold max quality time (cap 60s).
- Sessions keep similar structure but fewer sets; focus on perfect reps and control.

Progressions and Regressions
- Push-Ups:
  - Regression: hands elevated on countertop/sofa.
  - Progression: floor → feet elevated → pause at bottom → slow eccentrics.
- Pike Push-Ups (vertical push strength):
  - Regression: hands elevated, hips high.
  - Progression: feet on sofa, deeper ROM (books), slower eccentrics.
- Pull-Ups/Chin-Ups:
  - Regressions: foot or knee assist on chair; towel under foot; partial ROM; eccentric-only; isometric holds.
  - Progression: reduce assistance weekly; cluster singles; full reps.
- Rows:
  - Regression: higher body angle (more upright).
  - Progression: lower body angle, feet elevated, slow eccentrics, mid-range isometric.
- Squat/Lunge:
  - Progression via depth, pause, Bulgarians, front-foot elevation, AMRAP last set 1 RIR.
- Hip Hinge:
  - Patterning to single-leg RDL reach, hamstring walkouts, longer pauses at length.

Conditioning (Optional, 1–2x/week on non-lifting days, 12–18 min)
- Choose 2–3 low-impact options: brisk walk, step-ups on stairs, jump rope light, shadowboxing.
- Simple EMOM 12: 30s brisk stairs or marching in place; 30s easy. Keep nasal breathing. Do not compromise recovery for strength days.

Recovery and Mobility (Daily 5–10 min)
- After sessions: 2–3 min breathing, then stretch hip flexors, quads, hamstrings, lats/pecs (30–45s each).
- Elbow/shoulder care: forearm flexor/extensor stretches, scapular circles, 2–3x/week.
- Sleep: Aim 7.5–9 hours; consistent schedule.

Nutrition Guidelines (general for beginner male aiming for strength)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight daily, spread over 3–4 meals.
- Calories: Maintain slight surplus if body comp allows (+200–300 kcal/day) to support strength; if fat loss is desired, hold at maintenance while prioritizing protein.
- Carbs around training: 30–60 g 60–90 min pre-workout; similar post-workout; hydrate well.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily, any time, consistent. Plenty of water.
- Omega-3s and a basic vitamin D if intake/exposure is low (as per local guidance).

Technique Cues (key reminders)
- Create full-body tension: squeeze glutes, brace abs (exhale, then slight inhale, 360° brace).
- Pulling: lead with elbows down and back; avoid shrugging; keep ribcage down.
- Pushing: hands spread, corkscrew into floor; chest to object; neutral neck.
- Lower body: knee tracks over toes; full foot contact; slow controlled eccentrics.
- Chin-ups: start from active hang; pull chest toward bar; avoid kipping.

Tracking and Progress
- Keep a simple log: variation, sets x reps, RIR, tempo notes.
- Progress when top of rep range hit in all sets with 1–2 RIR; otherwise add reps before changing leverage.
- If stalling >2 weeks, step back one variation and rebuild with perfect form.

Safety
- Check doorway bar installation before every session.
- For rows under a table/chair: only if absolutely sturdy; otherwise stick to doorframe/towel rows.
- Stop sets 1–2 reps before form breaks; elbows and shoulders should feel stable, not painful.

Here’s a practical, beginner-friendly 12-week nutrition plan to pair with the training. It’s structured, flexible, and easy to execute from a small flat with minimal cooking. Adjust portions weekly based on progress.

Step 1: Set targets
- Goal: Build strength and lean muscle with minimal fat gain.
- Calories: Bodyweight (kg) × 33–36 kcal/day. If his weight is unknown, start at 2,600–2,800 kcal/day (average 27-year-old male). Adjust by 150–200 kcal based on weekly check-ins.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day (anchor at 2.0 g/kg for simplicity).
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day (don’t go below 0.6 g/kg).
- Carbs: Fill remaining calories after protein and fat.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add +500 ml on training days.

How to adjust weekly
- If weight is flat for 2 consecutive weeks and performance isn’t improving: +150–200 kcal (carbs first).
- If gaining >0.4 kg/week for 2 weeks and waist is expanding quickly: −150–200 kcal (from carbs).
- If feeling sluggish in sessions: add 25–50 g carbs in the 2–3 hours around training.

Meal timing (simple)
- 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks.
- Pre-workout (60–120 min prior): 30–60 g carbs + 20–40 g protein; low fat/fiber.
- Post-workout (within 2 hours): 30–80 g carbs + 25–40 g protein.
- Evenings: Emphasize protein, veggies, and slower-digesting carbs if training next morning.

Food framework (flexible “plates”)
- Protein options (rotate): eggs, Greek yogurt/skyr, cottage cheese, milk, whey/plant protein, chicken/turkey, lean beef, tuna/salmon/mackerel, tofu/tempeh, lentils/beans.
- Carb options: oats, rice, pasta, potatoes/sweet potatoes, wholegrain bread/wraps, quinoa, couscous, fruit, cereal.
- Fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts/nut butter, seeds, whole eggs, oily fish, dark chocolate.
- Veggies: aim 3–5 servings/day; include a colorful mix.
- Convenience: frozen veg/fruit, tinned fish/beans, ready rice/pouches, pre-cooked grains.

Portion guide (no scale needed)
- Protein: 2 palm-sized portions per main meal (1 palm ≈ 25–30 g protein).
- Carbs: 1–2 cupped-hand portions per main meal (more on training days).
- Fats: 1–2 thumb-sized portions per meal.
- Veg: 2 fist-sized portions/day minimum; more is better.

Sample day (≈2,700–2,800 kcal; ~180–190 g protein)
- Breakfast: Oats (80 g) cooked in milk, banana, whey (30 g), 1 tbsp peanut butter.
- Snack: Greek yogurt (300 g) + berries + honey.
- Lunch: Chicken wrap: 2 wholegrain wraps, 180 g cooked chicken, salad mix, salsa, olive oil drizzle.
- Pre-workout (if needed): Cereal bar + apple + 300 ml milk.
- Post-workout/Dinner: Salmon (200 g) with microwavable rice (250 g cooked) and frozen veg medley with olive oil.
- Evening snack: Cottage cheese (200 g) + dark chocolate (20–30 g) + kiwi.

Budget/simple swaps
- Protein: eggs, milk, yogurt, tinned tuna/mackerel, frozen chicken/thighs, lentils/beans.
- Carbs: oats, rice, pasta, potatoes, store-brand cereal, frozen fruit.
- Fats: olive oil, peanuts, mixed seeds.

Supplement guidance (optional, evidence-based)
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g daily, any time; expect 1–2 kg water weight increase early.
- Vitamin D3: 1,000–2,000 IU/day if sun exposure is low (confirm with local guidelines).
- Omega-3: 1–2 g combined EPA/DHA daily if oily fish <2x/week.
- Protein powder: Use to hit targets, not required.

12-week escalation and focus
- Weeks 1–2: Nail consistency. Hit protein target daily. Keep meals repeatable. Track bodyweight 3x/week (morning, after bathroom).
- Weeks 3–4: Tighten peri-workout carbs. Add fruit or easy carbs pre/post. Review weight trend; adjust calories ±150–200.
- Weeks 5–6: Increase fiber variety (5+ veg/fruit servings/day). Add 500–1,000 extra steps/day for appetite regulation.
- Weeks 7–8: Protein quality audit: include 2 servings of high-leucine protein/day (e.g., whey, milk, poultry, eggs).
- Weeks 9–10: Recovery push: 7.5–9 h sleep; add pre-bed protein (20–40 g casein/Greek yogurt).
- Weeks 11–12: Maintain intake that supported best training. If body fat gain feels high, trim carbs slightly on rest days (−25–50 g).

Pre/post-workout snack ideas (quick, no-cook)
- Pre (choose 1): banana + milk; yogurt + granola; toast + jam + whey shake; cereal bar + fruit.
- Post (choose 1): chocolate milk; tuna wrap; rice pouch + chicken pieces; whey + oats + fruit.

Hydration/electrolytes
- Start day with 300–500 ml water + pinch of salt or a squeeze of lemon.
- On hot days or if sweating more, add 1 electrolyte tablet or 1/4 tsp salt to 500–700 ml water.

Adherence checklist
- Hit protein target 6–7 days/week.
- Eat at least 3 meals/day.
- 5+ servings fruit/veg on 5 days/week.
- Drink 2–3 L water/day.
- Weigh-in 3x/week; weekly average is what you adjust from.
- One “free” meal per week is fine; keep protein high.

Here’s a simple, effective at-home cardio plan that complements the 12-week strength program, needs no extra equipment beyond the mat and doorway bar, and fits in a small flat. It focuses on low-impact options to protect joints and not interfere with strength gains.

How to schedule
- Frequency: 2 sessions per week to start (Weeks 1–4), up to 3 sessions per week by Weeks 5–12 if recovery and strength progress remain solid.
- Placement: On non-lifting days or at least 6–8 hours away from strength training. If on the same day, do cardio after lifting.
- Duration: 15–25 minutes per session early; up to 30 minutes later.
- Intensity guide: Use a 1–10 Rate of Perceived Exertion (RPE).
  - Easy/recovery: RPE 3–4 (nasal breathing, can speak in sentences).
  - Moderate/base: RPE 5–6 (can speak in short phrases).
  - Hard intervals: RPE 7–8 (few words).

Weekly structure by phase
- Weeks 1–4 (build base, low impact)
  - Session 1: Zone 2 base
    - 18–25 minutes continuous: brisk marching in place, step-ups on a single stair or sturdy step, shadowboxing light, or low-impact dance. Keep RPE 4–5, nasal breathing if possible.
  - Session 2: Technique + cadence
    - 6 rounds: 90s brisk marching or step-ups (RPE 5–6) + 30s fast feet in place or shadowboxing (RPE 7), 1-minute easy walk/march between rounds.
  - Optional finisher (5 minutes): Mobility flow (world’s greatest stretch, hip openers) to downshift and aid recovery.

- Weeks 5–8 (progress volume and add intervals)
  - Session 1: Steady state
    - 25–30 minutes continuous at RPE 5. Alternate movements every 5 minutes to avoid monotony: step-ups, marching, shadowboxing.
  - Session 2: Simple intervals (EMOM-style)
    - 16 minutes: every minute on the minute do 30s hard (RPE 7–8) + 30s easy (RPE 3–4). Rotate: fast step-ups, speed marching/high knees (low impact), shadowboxing flurries.
  - Optional Session 3 (only if recovery good): Low-intensity 20 minutes Zone 2 walk outdoors or marching with mobility breaks.

- Weeks 9–12 (intensify selectively; maintain low impact)
  - Session 1: Threshold builder
    - 4 x 4 minutes at upper steady pace (RPE 6–7) with 2 minutes easy between. Use step-ups or fast marching. Total ~24 minutes plus 3–5 minutes easy warm-up and cool-down.
  - Session 2: Power intervals
    - 10 rounds: 20s hard (RPE 8) + 40s easy (RPE 3–4). Movements: shadowboxing flurries, fast step-ups, mountain climbers (low-impact option: slow but forceful).
  - Optional Session 3: Recovery cardio
    - 15–20 minutes very easy (RPE 3–4) + 5 minutes breathing/mobility.

Warm-up and cool-down for every cardio session (5–6 minutes total)
- Warm-up (3 minutes): easy marching in place → arm circles → hip circles → 2 x 20s faster marching.
- Cool-down (2–3 minutes): slow march → nasal breathing in through nose/out through mouth, then light calf/hip flexor/pec stretch 20–30s each.

Exercise menu (rotate to keep it fresh)
- Marching in place (progress by cadence).
- Step-ups on a single stair or sturdy step (hold railing/wall for balance).
- Shadowboxing (add light slips, pivots; stay on forefeet).
- Fast feet in place (low amplitude).
- Low-impact high knees (drive knees without jumping).
- Mountain climbers (slow/controlled for low impact).
- Bear crawl in place (tiny steps forward/back, controlled).
- Skaters (low range) side-to-side without leaving the floor.
- Jump rope simulation (no rope): rhythmic heel-toe hops or marches.
- Stair climbing in building (if allowed/safe): keep RPE 5–6; hold rail.

Safety and form cues
- Keep joints happy: prioritize low-impact options; no forced jumping in a small space.
- Posture: tall torso, ribs down, soft knees; land softly.
- Step-ups: full foot on step, push through heel, control down.
- Shadowboxing: keep hands up, short combos, relaxed shoulders; don’t hyperextend elbows.

Progression rules
- Add 2–3 minutes to steady sessions once they feel easy two weeks in a row.
- For intervals, add 1 round every 1–2 weeks or increase hard effort by +1 RPE while keeping technique crisp.
- If strength sessions feel compromised, pull back cardio volume by 20–30% for a week.

Heart-rate guidance (optional if he tracks)
- Zone 2 target: roughly 60–70% max HR.
- Threshold sets: 75–85% max HR.
- If no HR monitor: default to the RPE and talk test guidelines above.

Recovery considerations
- Keep at least one full rest day/week with only an easy walk or mobility.
- Hydrate: 300–500 ml water before and after cardio; add a pinch of salt if very sweaty.

Here’s a fun, 20–30 minute “Saturday Finisher” he can do in a small flat with just the mat and doorway bar. It’s built as a rotating menu so it stays fresh, scales to his level, and won’t beat him up before the next training week. Choose one track each Saturday, or cycle A → B → C → D.

General rules
- Warm-up (4–5 min): easy march in place, arm circles, hip circles, 10 scap push-ups, 10 glute bridges, 20s fast feet.
- Intensity: Aim for RPE 6–8 (challenging but fun). Stop sets 1–2 reps before form breaks.
- Duration: 20–30 minutes total.
- Cool-down (3 min): slow march + 2–3 stretches (hip flexor, pecs/lats, calves).

Track A: “Pull-Up Playground”
Goal: make vertical pulling fun and progress chin-ups.

1) Skill ladder (10–12 min)
- 6 rounds, rest as needed between sets:
  - Option 1 (beginner): 1 assisted chin-up + 5s top hold + 5s eccentric
  - Option 2 (intermediate): 2 singles (lightest assist) + 8s eccentric on the second rep
  - Add 1–2s to the isometric each round if you can.

2) EMOM 8: Rows + Core
- Odd minutes: 20–30s doorframe/towel row (hard angle)
- Even minutes: 20–30s hollow body hold (tuck/one-leg/ full per level)

3) Fun finisher: “Dead Hang Dice”
- Roll a die or use a random-number app for seconds to hang (e.g., roll = 1 → 10s, 2 → 15s, … 6 → 35s). Do 4–5 rolls with 20–30s shake-out between.

Track B: “Push Party + Pump”
Goal: push-up skill and a satisfying upper-body pump without wrecking joints.

1) Mechanical drop set circuit (12–14 min, 3–4 rounds, 60–75s rest between rounds)
- A) Push-up hardest elevation x 4–6
- B) Immediately raise hands slightly x 4–6
- C) Immediately 15–20s mid-range isometric hold
- D) Prone Y-T-W x 6 each (control)

2) Triceps & delts cash-out (6–8 min)
- EMOM 6–8:
  - Odd: Pike handstand hold or downward-dog shoulder taps x 20–30s
  - Even: Close-grip push-ups at easier elevation x 6–10

3) Core tag
- 2 sets: side plank reach-throughs x 8–10/side, rest 30s

Track C: “Legs + Lungs Game”
Goal: lower-body burn plus cardio, all low-impact.

1) 15-minute ascending ladder
- Reverse lunge x 3/side
- Step-ups on a stair (or high-knee march) x 10 total
- Glute bridge x 10
- March in place fast x 20s
- Each round add +1 rep per side to lunges and +5 reps to step-ups/high-knees. Keep bridges at 10 and march at 20s. Stop at 15 minutes.

2) Hamstring finisher
- 3 sets: hamstring walkouts x 8–12 + 10s glute bridge iso hold; 45–60s rest

3) Optional: “Quad Coin Flip”
- Heads = 20s wall sit, Tails = 30s wall sit. Flip 3–4 times with 20s rest.

Track D: “Full-Body Flow Challenge”
Goal: move continuously, get a sweat, practice strength skills.

1) 20-minute AMRAP (as many quality rounds as possible; keep form crisp)
- 5–8 push-ups (choose elevation)
- 5 assisted chin-up reps total as cluster (e.g., 2 + 2 + 1)
- 8/side Bulgarian split squat or reverse lunge
- 10 slow mountain climbers/side (low impact)
- 20–30s hollow hold or 10 dead bugs/side
- 20–30s active hang or 10 scap pulls

Pacing tips
- Pick a sustainable pace for 10 minutes, then try to match or slightly beat it in minutes 10–20.
- If form slips, add 15–30s rest between movements.

Track E: “Core & Carry (No Carry)”
Goal: serious trunk work and grip without leaving the flat.

1) Anti-extension/rotation tri-set (3–4 rounds)
- Hollow rocks x 8–12
- Side plank hip lifts x 10/side
- Bear crawl in place x 20–30s (tiny steps forward/back), 45–60s rest

2) Grip and hang complexes (3 rounds)
- 20–30s dead hang
- 8–10 scapular pull-ups
- 10s chin-over-bar isometric
- Rest 60–90s

3) Finisher: slow Turkish get-up pattern without weight (or with a backpack)
- 2 reps/side, extremely slow and controlled

Scaling and variety
- Make it easier: shorten work intervals, raise push-up elevation, use more chin-up assistance, reduce ladder increments.
- Make it harder: lower hand elevation, add longer eccentrics/pauses, extend hangs, reduce rest, add backpack/weight vest when he gets one.

- Keep this as “fun hard,” not max-out. If Sunday feels sluggish, trim next Saturday to 15–20 minutes or stay in RPE 6–7.
- If elbows or shoulders are tender from the week, skip Track A/B and choose C or E.

Here’s a simple, effective mobility routine he can do in a small flat with just the mat. It targets hips, thoracic spine, ankles, shoulders, and wrists—areas that get tight from sitting and from the program’s push/pull/lunge work. Two formats: Daily Short (8–10 min) and Deeper Reset (20–25 min). Use the Short most days; do the Reset 1–2x/week or when stiff. All movements are controlled; breathe slowly through the nose.

General cues
- Tempo: Move slowly; 2–3s in/out of end ranges; no bouncing.
- Breath: Exhale into tight spots; 2–3 relaxed breaths in each end range.
- Range: Only to mild–moderate stretch (3–6/10); tension, not pain.
- Order: Spine/hips first, then ankles/shoulders, then finish with a downshift.

Daily Short (8–10 minutes)
1) Reset breathing (90/90 or crocodile) – 1 minute
- Lie on back, feet on wall or on floor, knees 90°. Inhale through nose, long slow exhale, feel ribs drop.

2) Cat–Camel – 6 slow reps
- Focus on segmental flexion/extension, smooth spine wave.

3) T-Spine Opener: Thread-the-Needle – 5 reps/side
- From quadruped, slide arm under, reach, then rotate open; keep hips stacked.

4) Hip 90/90 Switches – 8 reps alternating
- Sit in 90/90; smoothly switch sides without hands if possible; tall torso.

5) World’s Greatest Stretch (half-kneeling) – 3 cycles/side
- Lunge, back knee down: elbow-to-inside-ankle, T-spine rotation up, then hip flexor/hamstring rock.

6) Ankle Dorsiflexion Rock – 10 reps/side
- Half-kneeling, drive knee over toes keeping heel down; add 2s end-range pause.

7) Scapular CARs (controlled articular rotations) – 6 reps each direction
- Standing: shrug forward/up/back/down in big circles; slow and smooth.

8) Shoulder Opener: Doorway Pec Stretch – 2 x 20–30s/side
- Forearm on doorframe, gentle lean forward; keep ribs down.

9) Wrist Prep – 30–45s
- Hands on floor, fingers forward/back/side to side: gentle rocking in each position.

10) Downshift – 30–60s
- Child’s pose with long exhales or supine breathing with feet up.

Deeper Reset (20–25 minutes)
1) Breath + pelvic tuck – 2 minutes
- Supine, feet on wall, light posterior pelvic tilt; 4s inhale, 6–8s exhale.

2) Segmental Cat–Camel – 8 reps
- Try to move one vertebra at a time.

3) T-Spine Rotation Progression – 2 x 6/side
- Side-lying open book: knees stacked, rotate top arm across floor; add 2s end-range hold.

4) Hip Capsule/Glute: 90/90 with end-range isometrics – 2 rounds/side
- 20s gentle push (press shin into floor), then 10s pull (try to lift front ankle/shin), then relax deeper.

5) Hip Flexor + Quad – 2 x 30–40s/side
- Half-kneeling lunge, posterior pelvic tilt, glute squeeze; optional reach overhead/side-bend.

6) Hamstring Contract–Relax – 2 rounds/side
- Supine strap/towel hamstring stretch: 20s hold, 5s gentle push (heel down into towel), relax, pull 5–10° deeper.

7) Ankle Dorsiflexion with band/towel assist – 2 x 12 rocks/side
- Pull talus down/back with towel around ankle as you drive knee over toes; 1–2s pause.

8) Shoulder + Lats: Child’s Pose Side-Bend – 2 x 20–30s/side
- Hands to the right, sit back left hip; switch sides.

9) Scap/Shoulder Control
- Wall Slides with Posterior Tilt – 2 x 8–10 reps
- Prone Y-T-W (no weight) – 1–2 sets of 6–8 each, slow 2–3s holds.

10) Neck Hygiene – 60–90s total
- Gentle nods/turns; then upper-trap/levator stretch 20–30s/side (keep shoulders down).

11) Finish: Box Breathing – 1 minute
- 4–4–4–4 count; feel ribs expand 360°.

Pre-Session Mobility (3–5 minutes) to pair before lifting
- 30s crocodile breathing
- 4 Cat–Camels
- 3/side world’s greatest stretch
- 6 scap push-ups
- 8 glute bridges

Post-Session Downshift (4–6 minutes)
- 1 minute easy march or nasal breathing
- Hip flexor stretch 30s/side
- Doorway pec stretch 30s/side
- Calf/ankle stretch 30s/side
- 60–90s supine breathing (feet elevated)

Weekly mobility focus (rotate emphasis)
- Week 1: Hips/hamstrings (extra 90/90 work + hamstring CR)
- Week 2: Shoulders/T-spine (more open books + wall slides)
- Week 3: Ankles (extra dorsiflexion rocks, calf stretch holds)
- Week 4: Mixed deload (short routine daily)
- Repeat this 4-week focus in Phases 2 and 3.

Desk/phone “snacks” (30–60s, 2–3x/day)
- 10 neck nods/turns + 10 scap circles
- 10 ankle circles/leg pumps each side
- 5 deep nasal breaths with long exhales while standing tall

Safety and scaling
- If any position pinches or causes numbness, back off range or skip that drill.
- Keep ribs stacked over pelvis (avoid big low-back arches) during stretches.
- Consistency beats intensity; small daily doses work best.

- Session B: Tempo chair squat 6x4–5; pike push-up clusters 4 rounds (2–3 + 15–20s + 2–3); row 5x6 (4s down); hip thrust 4x8–10 (3s top, last set to 1 RIR); dead bug 3x10/side; wall slides 2x12
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 5x7–8/side; push-up mechanical drop set x3 rounds (hard 4–6 → easier 4–6 → 10–15s iso); chin-up partials top-half 5x2–3 then 1 slow 8–10s eccentric; walkouts 4x10–12; side plank hip lifts 3x10–12/side

Week 7
- Session A: Bulgarians 6x5/side (1s bottom); push-up strength 6x4–6 (3–4s down, 1s pause); chin-up singles 8–10 with least assist (3–4s down; last two add 2s top hold); single-leg RDL 4x6–8 (4s down); hollow rocks 3x12–18
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 7x3–4 (6s down, 2s pause); pike push-up 5x3–5 (4–5s down, last set AMRAP to technical limit); row 5x5–6 (4s down + 1s top pause); hip thrust 4x6–8 (3s top); dead bug 3x10/side
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 5x6–8/side (last set to 1 RIR); push-up eccentrics 4x3–5 (5–6s down + 2s pause) then 1 back-off AMRAP at easier elevation; chin-up eccentrics 6x2 (8–10s) + 1 max top hold; walkouts 4x10–12

Week 8 (deload/consolidate)
- Session A: Bulgarians 4x5–6; push-up 4x4–6 (same elevation); assisted chin-up 5x2–3; single-leg RDL 3x6–8; hollow 2x25–35s; active hang 2x30–40s
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 5x3–4 (4s down); pike push-up 4x3–5; row 4x6–8; hip thrust 3x8–10; dead bug 2x10/side
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 4x6–8/side; push-up back-off 3x6–10 (easier elevation); chin-up eccentrics 4x2 (6s); walkouts 3x8–10
- End-of-week markers: Max floor push-ups or lowest elevation; max assisted chin-ups set; Bulgarian split squat AMRAP to parallel (cap 20).

Phase 3: Intensification/Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: Push toward unassisted chin-ups, strong floor push-ups, deeper single-leg strength; slightly lower volume with higher difficulty.

Week 9
- Session A: Bulgarians 5x6/side (last set AMRAP to 1 RIR); push-up floor or low elev. 5x5–8; chin-up clusters: 5 rounds of (1–2 reps, 20–30s, 1–2 reps); hip thrust 4x8–10 (3s final rep hold); hollow 3x25–35s; active hang 3x30–45s
- Session B: Tempo chair squat 6x4 (5s down); pike push-up (deficit if ready) 4x5–6; horizontal row hard angle 4x6–8; single-leg RDL 4x8/side (2s bottom); dead bug 3x10/side; scap wall slides 2x10
- Session C: FFE reverse lunge 4x10/side; diamond push-up (appropriate elevation) 4x6–8; chin-up eccentrics 6x2 (6–8s) + 1 timed chin-over-bar hold; walkouts 3x10–12; side plank hip lifts 3x10/side

Week 10
- Add +1 rep/set on push-ups if clean (or feet elevation/pauses if at 8s). Accumulate 30+ total chin-up reps (mix clusters/assists/eccentrics). Lower: deeper ROM or +1 rep, last set AMRAP 1 RIR for Bulgarians/lunges. Keep rows/pike challenging via tempo.

Week 11
- Strength emphasis (lower reps, higher difficulty):
  - Push-up: 6x4–6 (2–3s down, brief bottom pause)
  - Chin-up: 8–10 singles (least assist) with 60–90s rest; last two add 5–10s top hold
  - Rows: 5x6 (4s down)
  - Lower body: 4–5x6–8 (tempo/ROM)
  - Core: Hollow rocks 3x12–20; tall-kneeling anti-rotation press (towel vs doorframe) 3x10s/side

Week 12 (peak/test/deload blend)
- Reduce sets by ~30%, keep effort high (1–2 RIR). Test mid-week:
  - Max clean floor push-ups
  - Chin-up status: 1 unassisted? If not, max assisted + best 8–10s eccentric
  - Split squat AMRAP to parallel (cap 25)
  - Hollow hold max quality time (cap 60s)
- Keep similar exercise menu with fewer sets; emphasize perfect control.

Cardio plan (fits all phases)

Mobility routine
- Daily Short (8–10 min): breathing reset → cat-camel → thread-the-needle → hip 90/90 switches → world’s greatest stretch → ankle rocks → scap CARs → doorway pec stretch → wrist prep → downshift.
- Deeper Reset (20–25 min, 1–2x/week): adds open book, contract–relax for hips/hamstrings, hip flexor/quad, ankle assist, wall slides, Y-T-W, neck hygiene, box breathing.

Nutrition overview (pair with training)
- Calories: BW(kg) × 33–36 kcal/day (or start ~2,600–2,800 kcal/day); adjust ±150–200 kcal based on 2-week trends.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day (anchor ~2.0 g/kg). Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day. Carbs: remainder.
- Timing: 3 meals + 1–2 snacks; 30–60 g carbs + 20–40 g protein pre; 30–80 g carbs + 25–40 g protein post.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; +500 ml on training days.
- Supplements (optional): creatine 3–5 g/day; vitamin D if low sun; omega-3 if oily fish <2x/week; protein powder to fill gaps.
- 12-week focus: Weeks 1–2 consistency; Weeks 3–4 peri-workout carbs; Weeks 5–6 fiber variety; Weeks 7–8 leucine-rich protein; Weeks 9–10 sleep + pre-bed protein; Weeks 11–12 maintain intake that fuels best training.

Equipment roadmap (if he wants to buy later)
- Tier 1: Adjustable dumbbells (aim up to 20–25 kg each), resistance bands with door anchor, gymnastic rings (hang from bar).
- Tier 2: One heavy kettlebell (24–28 kg) + one moderate (12–16 kg), adjustable weight vest (10–20 kg+).
- Tier 3: Short/loadable bar + plates, folding bench, recovery tools.

Safety and tracking
- Check doorway bar stability every session; avoid under-table rows unless the furniture is unquestionably sturdy.
- Log variation, sets x reps, tempo, RIR, and assistance level (for chins). Progress when all sets hit the top of the range with 1–2 RIR.
- If stalled >2 weeks, step back one variation, rebuild with perfect form, and ensure nutrition/sleep support training.
